question: What is the main purpose of conducting a community diagnosis?

options.A: To test new pharmaceutical drugs on healthy village residents
options.B: To replace traditional healers with western medical doctors
options.C: To identify health needs and available resources in a population
options.D: To punish local leaders for poor environmental sanitation

explanation: A community diagnosis looks at both the health gaps and the existing assets of a population to guide future interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why is a community diagnosis compared to an individual physical examination?

options.A: Because nurses must examine every single resident physically
options.B: Because community members are treated inside a hospital ward
options.C: Because diagnosis always requires a laboratory blood test
options.D: Because health problems must be assessed before treatment is planned

explanation: Just as a clinician diagnoses an individual patient before giving medicine, public health workers assess a community to design the right health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h1)

question: What is the first crucial step before collecting data in a new community?

options.A: Writing a final report for the federal ministry of health
options.B: Administering mass vaccinations to all children under five
options.C: Demolishing illegal structures that block drainage systems
options.D: Community entry and gaining the trust of local leaders

explanation: Without properly introducing the team to local leaders and gaining entry, residents may be uncooperative and data collection will fail. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h2)

question: Why must health workers meet with community chiefs and leaders during the preparatory phase?

options.A: To demand financial contributions from the village treasury
options.B: To appoint new political leaders for the local government
options.C: To secure cooperation and reduce suspicion from residents
options.D: To force them to sign legal contracts for clinic construction

explanation: Involving community leaders early builds trust, ensuring that the people willingly participate in the upcoming health assessment. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which data collection method involves walking through the community to visually inspect environmental conditions?
explanation: Observation or windshield surveys allow nurses to physically see housing conditions, water sources, and waste disposal practices. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: A nurse wants to understand why mothers in a village refuse to bring children for immunization. Which method is most suitable?

options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccine vials
options.C: Measuring the mid-upper arm circumference of infants
options.D: Counting the number of houses in the ward

explanation: Group discussions allow community members to freely share cultural beliefs, fears, and reasons behind specific health behaviors. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: What must be done immediately after collecting raw data from a community survey?

options.A: Dismissal of all community health committees
options.B: Immediate closure of all local markets

explanation: Collected data must be sorted and analyzed to reveal patterns, rates, and actual health needs before planning interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h4)

question: How do nurses determine if a specific disease rate in a community is a serious problem?

options.A: By waiting for international agencies to declare an emergency
options.B: By checking how many doctors are currently on duty
options.C: By comparing local rates with regional or national standards
options.D: By asking traditional healers for their personal opinions

explanation: Comparing local health data against established benchmarks helps nurses identify which conditions require urgent public health attention. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following is a key criterion used to prioritize community health problems?

options.A: Distance from the capital city international airport
options.B: Magnitude or number of people affected
options.C: The political party affiliation of the village head
options.D: The architectural design of the local health clinic

explanation: Magnitude measures how widespread a health issue is, helping planners focus on problems affecting the largest segments of the population. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why is it necessary to involve community members when prioritizing health problems?

options.A: To ensure they take ownership and support the chosen interventions
options.B: To shift all financial responsibilities away from the government
options.C: To prove that health workers are superior planners
options.D: To delay the project until funding runs out

explanation: When people help choose which problem to tackle first, they are much more likely to participate actively in solving it. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary output of the action planning phase?

options.A: A lengthy academic textbook published for university students
options.B: An application for international political asylum
options.C: A detailed schedule of activities, responsibilities, and resources
options.D: A list of punishments for families who violate hygiene laws

explanation: An action plan clearly outlines what tasks need to be done, who is responsible, when it will occur, and what materials are needed. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: A community action plan includes assigning specific tasks to local youth groups. What is the main benefit of this?

options.A: It guarantees that international donors will send more money
options.B: It builds local capacity and ensures project sustainability
options.C: It eliminates the need for any monitoring or supervision
options.D: It prevents the nurses from doing any actual field work

explanation: Involving local groups builds their skills and ensures the community can maintain the health interventions long after external nurses leave. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h6)

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation in community health programs?

options.A: Monitoring deals only with finance, while evaluation deals only with drugs
options.B: Monitoring is done only by doctors, while evaluation is done by patients
options.C: Monitoring is ongoing during the project, while evaluation assesses final outcomes
options.D: Monitoring happens after the project closes, while evaluation happens before

explanation: Monitoring happens continuously as activities are implemented, whereas evaluation measures the ultimate success or impact of the project at the end. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)

question: Why is final reporting to the community an essential final step?

options.A: To prove to the government that the nurses deserve a salary raise
options.B: To fulfill a legal requirement so nurses can travel abroad
options.C: To advertise private clinics opening in nearby towns
options.D: To maintain transparency and respect for community participation

explanation: Feeding results back to the community shows respect, maintains trust, and encourages continued community-driven health maintenance. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h7)
